situation: My dog Rufus died last Tuesday and the house is too quiet without his collar jingling in the hall.
poem:
The hall gives back no jingle now,
and Rufus is a quiet with a name.
His collar on its hook, his bowl put by,
and every room a little too much room.

situation: The letter came today: I have been accepted to the marine biology program in Bergen.
poem:
The word came, and the word was yes,
and all the shut doors opened in a row.
You will go far and learn the greener things,
and come back glittering with what you know.

situation: My mother's biopsy results come back on Friday and I have cleaned the kitchen three times.
poem:
Friday keeps the envelope with your mother's name,
and the kitchen shines from all your frightened hands.
Sit down. Stop scrubbing. Breathe until it comes.
The waiting is the worst of it, always.

situation: I have been waiting at the DMV in chair forty-two for two hours and my number still has not been called.
poem:
The room is grey and holds you where you sit,
and the hours do not move, and do not move.
A voice goes calling out into the air,
and the afternoon lies down and will not rise.

situation: My landlord kept my whole deposit for one scuff on the baseboard and will not answer his phone.
poem:
The money's gone for one small mark of scuff,
and he will not pick up, and will not pick up.
Take him to court. Send the letter tomorrow.
You are right to burn. Burn a little.

situation: The tornado passed two streets over and our oak tree is still standing.
poem:
The great noise passed and did not choose us,
and everything we love is standing yet.
The sky washes itself and goes on blue,
and we are lucky, lucky, and alive.

situation: I burned the first pancake again, the way my grandmother always did, and the smoke alarm went off.
poem:
The first of anything is for the fire,
and we are old friends with our small ruin.
A little failure, warm and brown and kind,
and then the day comes right the second time.

situation: My daughter Maya took her first steps across the kitchen tile this morning, straight into the dog's water bowl.
poem:
Maya goes out across the kitchen floor,
and finishes her journey in the water.
The dog's bowl throws its silver everywhere,
and no one in the house will stop laughing.

situation: I sold my father's blue Volvo yesterday and forgot to take the pine air freshener off the mirror.
poem:
Blue car, blue evening, and the pine still swinging,
gone off down the road in someone's hands.
You forgot the small tree on the mirror,
and your father goes with it, and is gone.

situation: I have to give a toast at my brother's wedding on Saturday and I have rewritten it eleven times.
poem:
So many drafts, and none of them will hold,
and still the day is coming with its music.
The words will do their stumbling work,
and everyone will hear the love beneath.

situation: It has rained for six days and I have reread the same page of my library book four times.
poem:
Grey and grey, and the days all stuck together,
and nothing in the world worth turning to.
The hours sit. The mind slides off and off.
O dull wet week without an edge to it.

situation: Someone keyed my car in the grocery store lot while I was inside buying milk.
poem:
A long white wound along the door's blue side,
dug while you paid for milk inside the store.
Some coward's hand, some quick and ugly minute,
and now the hot red thing that will not sit.

situation: My flight from Denver landed twenty minutes before the blizzard closed the runway. I have never been so glad to see a jetway.
poem:
You came down just before the door swung shut,
and the white came on behind you like a wall.
A little margin, and you are inside and warm,
and the cold can do its worst without you now.

situation: I found a five dollar bill in my winter coat pocket along with a movie ticket from last February.
poem:
The year hands back a little of its luck,
unlooked for, in the dark of something old.
Small mercies keep their places and wait,
and gladden the grey middle of a day.

situation: My best friend Priya moved to Auckland on Sunday and we finished the last of the chili in her freezer.
poem:
Priya took the long flight out on Sunday,
and the chili is finished, and the freezer hums.
Auckland gets her mornings and her laughing,
and here the kitchen keeps her empty chair.

situation: After eleven months of looking, I start the new job at the bakery on Monday.
poem:
Eleven months of asking, and a yes at last,
and Monday smelling warm of yeast and crust.
The bakery will take your two good hands,
and give them something worth the doing.

situation: My son has not texted back in three days and his last message was just a period.
poem:
Three days of silence after one grey period,
and the phone lies heavy as a stone.
Call him. Do not wait for him to call.
The quiet is a weight; put it down.

situation: I finally fixed the squeaking gate with a bit of olive oil because I could not find the WD-40.
poem:
The small annoyance of the house is gone,
and something that complained is quiet now.
Such easy work, and such a clean reward,
and the day goes on a little smoother for it.

situation: My coworker Dan presented my spreadsheet in the Tuesday meeting and never once said my name.
poem:
Dan read your work aloud and kept your name,
folded and pocketed and never said.
The room gave him its nodding and its thanks,
and you sat still and burned in the grey light.

situation: The cat came back after four nights out, thin and loud, and slept twelve hours on my sweater.
poem:
The lost came back out of the dark at last,
and the fear goes out of the house like smoke.
Something sleeps now where the worry sat,
and the long night is finally over.
